main_diagnosis: The pure scaled-softplus parameter transform introduced in the current iteration has caused a performance regression from the best-known NLE≈-529 (n_sub=4) to NLE≈-556, worse even than the n_sub=1 baseline of -548. The unbounded support of raw softplus spreads SBI prior mass across epidemiologically implausible regions (very high or near-zero beta/gamma), making it harder for NLE to learn an identifiable likelihood surface. The fix is to replace the unbounded softplus transform with a sigmoid-bounded transform that constrains parameters to known COVID-19 epidemiological ranges.

issues.description: The pure scaled-softplus transform (beta = softplus(raw)*0.40, gamma = softplus(raw)*0.15) is unbounded above, allowing SBI to explore beta>1.5/day or gamma>0.6/day — rates incompatible with any observed COVID-19 trajectory. This wastes simulator budget on implausible regions and degrades the NLE likelihood surface. Performance dropped to -556 from the best-known -529, confirming the transform change is the primary regression cause.
issues.suggestion: Replace with a sigmoid-bounded transform that enforces epidemiologically valid ranges: beta = 0.05 + 0.75 * sigmoid(raw_beta)  [range ~0.05–0.80/day, covering R0 1–8] and gamma = 0.03 + 0.37 * sigmoid(raw_gamma)  [range ~0.03–0.40/day, infectious period 2.5–33 days]. Use sigmoid(x) = 1/(1+exp(-x)) with the same two-branch numerical stability trick for |x|>20. This gives bounded, smooth, monotone transforms with non-vanishing gradients and concentrates SBI's search within the plausible parameter space, which should recover and improve upon the -529 NLE score.

issues.description: With the current parameter transform causing implausible trajectories (high beta or very low gamma), many simulated trajectories reach S≈0 or I≈0 within 10–20 steps, producing degenerate near-constant tails. These degenerate trajectories dominate the NLE training set and flatten the learned likelihood surface, making posterior concentration impossible regardless of n_sub. This is a secondary effect of the transform issue but compounds the NLE degradation.
issues.location: forward() — tau-leaping loop and early-exit guard (~line 140-195)
issues.suggestion: After fixing the parameter transform to bounded ranges, add a soft absorbing guard: if S_sub < 1 and I_sub < 1, break immediately without further sub-steps (already partially present but relies on I_sub==0 only). Additionally, consider logging an internal epidemic_extinct flag and returning it as metadata so SBI can down-weight degenerate trajectories during likelihood estimation. If the bounded transform is adopted, the incidence of such trajectories should drop sharply and the n_sub=4 sub-stepping should recover its -529 performance.
